title: Today's the Day:
title_short: Giving ShoesDay · Day-of match push · ALT (shoe costume)
headline: Giving ShoesDay is happening right now and every gift is matched: the same cards as the 4EveryKid version, told with the shoe costume for fun.
story: Same text, same card timing as the 4EveryKid version (13330664171), so Soles4Souls can compare them side by side. Only the picture changes: the shoe costume, funniest moments first.

Loops: L1 “Today is the day for what?” opens at 0:00 and closes at about 0:06 with TODAY IS GIVING SHOESDAY. L2 “Can we reach 2,500 kids before the day ends?” stays open to the CTA. Stakes: gifts are doubled today only, and the goal has to be hit before midnight.
Energy builds card by card and the cuts get faster. Not a general awareness video.
do: Text on screen from frame 1: TODAY IS THE DAY over a 2-second montage of the funniest costume moments.
Same cards, same words, same timing as the 4EveryKid version.
Shoe-costume B-roll only. One or two kid reactions from the happy kids folder are fine for the button.
Put the two match cards on their own track.
dont: No logo, wordmark or name card at 0:00. The wordmark is already on the end slide.
No extra logo on the end slide.
No Christmas imagery: no Santa, no Christmas trees, no “Merry Christmas”.
No stock footage. Client footage only.

Happy kids B-roll (Drive copy of Canto VPMCH) · Canto O2NNR · Canto VPMCH
Giving ShoesDay is Tuesday 1 December. Goal: 2,500 kids with new shoes. The Giving ShoesDay match is not confirmed yet.
Sydney's holiday end slide: V1 light blue or V2 dark blue. 1081×1921 JPG, 9:16. The SOLES4SOULS wordmark is already at the top. Put the CTA text in the open middle. No extra logo.
S4S graphics package (Drive). Same folder as the end slides. Type the words on the empty plates in Roboto. The logo files there are for end cards only; this campaign's end card is the holiday slide.
S4S teal #62CCBF, black, white, off-white #F8FAF9. Titles in Buenos Aires (Roboto Black if you do not have it), body in Roboto. Black text on teal. Never white on teal.
tech: Phone clips (MOV and MP4) from the Canto shoe-costume folder. Sizes and frame rates are mixed: check each on import.
1080×1920 at 23.976 fps (24p, Nick's brief). Conform 30 and 60 fps clips on purpose. Use the high frame rate only for slow motion you choose.
Horizontal clips: center-crop to 9:16 with the faces in frame. A 9:16 crop of 4K is 1215 px wide: punch-ins up to 120% stay sharp. No stretching.
No voice. Music plus natural sound (kids laughing, cheering) under it where it helps.
The two match cards (00:10 and 00:14) sit on their own track so they come out in one move.

Every on-screen line word for word from the script. Big, readable on a phone. Short cards, centered, out of the bottom 20% and away from the right edge (Instagram buttons). Hold each card long enough to read twice. Roboto Black for titles.
−14 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP peak. Music from licensed sources only. No swearing on screen or on the track.
H.264 MP4, 1080×1920. One file, 9:16 only. Upload to Frame.io with the Edit Key in the file name.
checklist: TODAY IS THE DAY is on screen at frame 1 and does not animate on. No logo at 0:00.
Every card matches the script word for word: Soles4Souls, Giving ShoesDay, 4EveryKid spelled right. US English.
TODAY IS THE DAY and TODAY IS GIVING SHOESDAY are in caps, as written.
The two match cards sit on their own track.
Text is big enough to read on a phone, out of the bottom 20% and away from the right edge.
Picture is the shoe costume; at most two kid reaction shots from the happy kids folder.
Ends on Sydney's holiday slide with Donate today: link in bio or s4s.org in the open middle. No extra logo.
Music is licensed, levels even, no clipping.

decisions.b: Sydney's doc holds the match lines until the Giving ShoesDay match is confirmed. Build V1 with both match cards on their own track. Nick is confirming with Sydney.

client_note: Why this matters: Giving ShoesDay (1 Dec) is Soles4Souls' biggest day of the year. Sydney wrote every line herself: keep it joy themed and positive.
